info.bio:
Hay dos artistas conocidos como Roy Brown: el bluesman y el puertorriqueño Roy Brown Ramirez. Esta página corresponde al primero.
------------------

Roy Brown (10 septiembre 1925 — 25 mayo 1981) fue un músico de blues que trasladó un estilo de cantar soul (desde la música gospel) hasta el emergente género del rock and roll.

scenes.name: Antecedentes (1892-1950)
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Antes del rock'n'roll: Tin Pan Alley, los primeros discos de blues (Mamie Smith) y de «old-time music», el yodel de Jimmie Rodgers, el crooning de Bing Crosby, el boogie-woogie, el jump blues de Louis Jordan (nacimiento de facto del rhythm'n'blues), la guitarra jazzística de T-Bone Walker, Woody Guthrie como primer gran cantautor y la exótica de Les Baxter. En paralelo, la vanguardia clásica (Russolo, Satie, Varèse, Cage, Schaeffer) anticipa el ruido, el ambient y la electrónica.

podcast.title: Post-Music Career and Death (1981)
podcast.body: After enjoying success in the late 1940s and very early 1950s, Brown spent decades unable to secure a hit. He eventually began selling encyclopedias door-to-door, using the unique marketing tactic of offering autographed photos of himself in black neighborhoods. He continued to release occasional R&B records but earned more from his encyclopedia sales before his death in 1981. "He eventually started selling in Cyclopidia's door to door, with the unique gimmick that when he was in black neighborhoods, he could offer the people whose doors he was knocking on, a nautical raft photo of himself."

podcast.title: "Good Rockin' Tonight" - New Orleans Recording, Non-New Orleans Sound
podcast.body: Despite being recorded in New Orleans and engineered by Cosimo Matassa, Roy Brown's "Good Rockin' Tonight" is categorized as Coastal Jump Band music and does not possess the characteristic "New Orleans sound." "It's of the type we're referring to as Coastal Jump Band music."

podcast.title: Difficulty with Record Companies
podcast.body: Roy Brown developed a reputation for being "difficult" after he sought assistance from the Musicians' Union to recover money owed to him by his record company. This led to a period in the 1950s where he struggled to achieve hit records. "Roy Brown got a reputation for being difficult. After he went to the musician's union to try to get some of the money the record company owed him."

podcast.title: Early Vocal Style and Influences
podcast.body: Initially, Brown's vocal style was distinct, leading him to be hired as a "black singer who sounds white," which was unusual given his frequent use of melisma, a characteristic typically associated with black singing. His primary vocal influences were crooners like Bing Crosby, rather than traditional blues artists. "Brown's main vocal influences when he started were people like Bing Fosby and other crewners, rather than blues music."

podcast.title: Fan of Wynonie Harris
podcast.body: Roy Brown was a significant admirer of Wynonie Harris and performed as a blues singer, often in a similar style to Harris. "Roy Brown was a big fan of Harris and was a blues singer himself. In something like the same style."

podcast.title: Move from Galveston to New Orleans
podcast.body: Roy Brown relocated back to New Orleans from Galveston, Texas, where he had been performing, due to unspecified personal reasons involving "a girl, and a club owner." "But after Brown moved back to New Orleans from Galveston, Texas, where he'd been performing, there was a girl, and a club owner, and these things happen and sometimes you have to move."

podcast.title: Offer to Wynonie Harris (Rejected)
podcast.body: Brown composed "Good Rockin' Tonight," believing in its popular potential. He offered the song to Wynonie Harris when Harris was performing in town, but Harris expressed no interest at that time. "Brown suggested the song to him, and Harris wasn't interested."

podcast.title: Shift to Rhythm and Blues
podcast.body: Brown soon developed a profound appreciation for rhythm and blues music, subsequently beginning to compose his own songs within this genre. "However, he soon became very fond of drum blues and started writing songs in the style himself."
